title: On the Origin of Beyond-Classical Advantage in the Parity-Permutation Problem
summary: We investigate the task of identifying the parity (odd vs even) of an unknown permutation applied to $n$ particles. Classically, using fewer than $n$ distinct labels per particle limits the success probability to random guessing, whereas quantum mechanics, exploiting entanglement in both preparation and measurement, accomplishes the task perfectly with as few as $\big\lceil \sqrt{n}\big\rceil$ levels per particle [\href{https://doi.org/10.1103/yhyv-xnwq}{PRL {\bf 135}, 260603 (2025)}].
